Project: Asset Management Policy and Plan Update
Description: The Township published its Asset Management Plan (AMP) in 2018 and affirmed a commitment to asset management through its Asset Management Policy (AM Policy) in 2019. The Ontario Regulation for Asset Management Planning for Municipal Infrastructure, O.Reg 588/17, requires municipalities to engage in forward planning for asset capital investment needs. Starting from July 1, 2024, municipalities are required to define current Levels of Service and Lifecycle Activities for all assets, both core and non-core. This work builds upon previous work completed by the Township, including existing asset and asset management knowledge, to ensure a complete understanding of context, cost-effective delivery, and effective use of Township time and resources. The Consultant's scope of work for this project will ensure that asset classes are addressed with appropriate Levels of Service, planned Lifecycle Activities, identify Asset Retirement Obligations and Financial Plans. The Township requires expert guidance on the implications of this regulatory change and information to support decisions on how best to manage trade-offs between services, risks, and costs going forward. In all, the Township needs to plan for the assets that require investment through an asset management plan, to identify sustainable, efficient actions that will aid in maintaining municipal services for the next 10 years.

Description: The Recipient will upgrade an existing Water Treatment Plant (317 First Street, at the intersection of First Street and River Ave E.The scope of work includes the installation of a new generator set to ensure reliable backup power during outages. Four chemical pumps will be replaced to maintain effective chemical dosing processes. Five 20-horsepower motors on the turbine pumps will be replaced with variable speed motors to allow for improved energy efficiency and better control over pumping operations. The control panel will be upgraded to modern standards to support improved system monitoring and automation. The clear wells will be cleaned, and their associated valves replaced to restore flow efficiency and storage integrity. The filters within the plant will be re-bedded to enhance filtration performance, and the settling tubes will be replaced to improve the sedimentation process. Project: Reconstruction of Renfrew Water Treatment Plant Dual Media High-Rate Gravity Filters
Description: The Recipient will rehabilitate the filtration component of the drinking water treatment plant in the Town of Renfrew. The project will consist of reconstructing the original two filters (Filters No. 1 and No. 2) by replacing their concrete launders with steel or carbon fibre alternatives and rehabilitation of the exterior walls with new concrete and waterproof membrane.  The filter media in filters No.2 & No.3 will be replaced to an approximate depth of 3’3” with a new optimized filter media design to improve compatibility with the upstream Actiflo clarification pretreatment. Underdrains in all three of the system filters will be replaced with new Phoenix 316L stainless steel laterals (or equivalent). Engineering review of the filters’ base will also occur prior to the installation of the new underdrains.The work on filters No.1 and No.2 will include removal of filter media; replacement of launders with 316 L stainless steel or carbon fibre launders (two per filter); reconstruction of the filters’ walls by removing the existing concrete substrate to an approximately 2" depth, roughening the concrete substrate and placing new concrete; and, reinstating or replacing the filter media. Each filter covers a 34.82 m2 area of 4.57 m x 7.62 m. Testing and commissioning of the reconstructed filtration system will also be done.The outcomes of this water infrastructure project will improve health and safety and promote the preservation of the current housing supply within the community

Description: The Town of Shelburne will undertake critical upgrades and expansion to the Water Pollution (Wastewater) Control Plant (WPCP) to accommodate growth from new industrial, commercial and residential developments. Description: Design and replacement of mechanical screen; including a bagger, screenings collection bin, and an electrical & control panel. With this system, operators will no longer be involved in picking up screenings manually. The existing headworks enclosure will be replaced with a new FRP enclosure large enough to contain the new mechanical screen components and heating and ventilation equipment. However, forredundancy, a manual bar screen will be added to the channel to avoid any overflowing or bypassing to downstream treatment units without screening.  The existing mechanical aerators will be removed and replaced with fine-bubble diffused aeration. One or two duty blowers will be considered together with provision of a standby blower along with manifolds, air supply piping and fine bubble diffusers.The new aeration system will include DO sensors and VFDs to control the air blowers based on dissolved oxygen concentration inside the aeration tanks, thereby optimizing power consumption of the plant. The work will be staged to complete removal of existing surface aerators and installation of the new aeration system in one aeration tank, while directing the flow to the other tank. Once the new aerators are commissioned and operational, flow will be switched to the refurbished tank and work will begin in the other tank. The aeration tanks should be cleaned when out of service to remove any accumulated rags and sludge. Install the blowers outdoors. A new secondary clarifier mechanism will be replaced.  The existing FRP enclosure on top of the clarifier tank will be removed for replacement of the existing mechanism. Since there is only one clarifier tank, the replacement of its mechanism requires the clarification system to be removed from service. Lagoon dredging was completed in summer of 2024. The alum storage tank will be replaced with a smaller PVC tank with consideration for provision of heating for the tank. Tendering process was completed in Aug-2024 with anticipated construction to begin early spring of 2025.
